title: Personal background; family origins
description: The interviewee provides her personal details, including her name, birth date, and residence in Elk River. She shares details about her mother Harriet Yager and her father John Morris, including their ages, marriage dates, and her father's work as a pharmacist.

title: Rural life pros and cons; rural versus urban life
description: Susan discusses the advantages of rural living, focusing on self-reliance and access to nature, while acknowledging issues like gossip and sewage systems. She compares her life with that of urban women, noting that rural women often face boredom and fewer scheduled activities, especially in winter.

title: Childhood play; community expectations
description: Susan reflects on her childhood as a tomboy playing outdoors with boys. She discusses how most local girls traditionally married right out of high school, though she notes a recent increase in those choosing to pursue college instead.

title: Education and college; hobbies and recreation; marriage expectations
description: Susan explains her switch from an animal science major to general studies. She describes her love for outdoor activities and family trips. She also mentions that her parents never pressured her to marry young, despite her being the only single woman of her age in town.

title: Family support; community activities; sewing
description: Susan talks about her household chores and working summer jobs to support her college tuition. She shares her history of participating in 4-H and the local Elk River Days festival. She also notes that her grandmother is the family expert in sewing and quilting.

title: Adjusting to rural life; local attitudes; media consumption
description: Susan advises city dwellers to be proactive in finding recreation and warns against acting superior when moving to a rural town. She critiques outsiders who stereotype rural residents as uneducated. She also discusses her family's magazine, radio, and television habits.

title: Future plans; small town schooling; fights and dating
description: Susan explains why she returned to Elk River after college and her future desires to travel, marry, and have a small family. She describes her experience in a tiny graduating class, the prevalence of school cliques, physical fights between girls, and dating norms.

title: School sports; curriculum gaps; parental roles
description: The conversation covers school sports, especially the success of the basketball and track teams. Susan points out the lack of math classes and electives in her high school curriculum. She also argues that parents often discourage students from attending college to save money.

title: Post-graduation paths; logging economy; divorce attitudes
description: Susan discusses how limited options lead many local girls into early marriages and subsequent divorces. She explains the dominant logging economy and how her pharmacist father encouraged his children to seek broader horizons. Finally, she describes how the community has become more accepting of divorce.
